answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in a cryptographic attestation chain verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Validating each node in the identity atlas requires staked collateral scaled to network density: individual nodes graze freely across the trust meadow, but coordinating counterfeit identities up the verification terrace triggers exponential capital exhaustion. Attacker cost scales as O(k^n), rendering massive swarms economically unfeasible.
